entitySuffixRule: Must contain the words "limited liability company" or "limited company," or the abbreviations "L.L.C.," "LLC," "L.C.," or "LC." The word "Limited" may be abbreviated "Ltd." and "Company" may be abbreviated "Co."
distinguishabilityNote: Must be distinguishable upon the records of the Secretary of State from the name of any corporation, limited partnership, limited liability partnership, or limited liability company incorporated, organized, or authorized to transact business in West Virginia, from a name reserved or registered under §§ 31B-1-106 or 31B-1-107 or under W. Va. Code §§ 31-1-12 or 31-1-13, and from a fictitious name approved under § 31B-10-1005 for a foreign company whose real name is unavailable. "Distinguishable" is defined in W. Va. Code § 31B-1-101(6), not in the naming section itself, and it has two prongs: at least a one-word difference when the words are common terms and the company is or might appear to be in a similar business, and at least a word order difference when the differing word is a proper name or an unusual term or when the company is clearly in a different type of business. A name that is not distinguishable may be used only if the present user, registrant, or owner consents in a record and submits an undertaking to change its own name, or if the applicant delivers a certified copy of a final judgment establishing its right to the name (§ 31B-1-105(c)). Separately, § 31B-1-105(d) lets a company use another company's name outright where it has merged with that company, been formed by reorganization with it, or acquired substantially all of its assets including the name.

notes: West Virginia adopted the Uniform Limited Liability Company Act (W. Va. Code ch. 31B). The statutory definition of "distinguishable" is in § 31B-1-101(6), the definitions section, not in § 31B-1-105, and it is two-pronged rather than a single one-word rule: a one-word difference is required where the words are common terms and the businesses look similar, and a word order difference where the differing word is a proper name or an unusual term. The Secretary of State's "Guidance for Selecting Business Organization Names in West Virginia" quotes that definition and then applies twelve non-exclusive tests on top of it, including a phonetic test, a billboard test, an industry test, and a punctuation test, and warns that a one-word difference is not always enough ("Capitol Letters, Inc." against "Capital Letters, Inc."). The Act itself has no statutory banned-word list; the restricted terms recorded here come from the guidance document's misleading-name test, which refuses names implying governmental affiliation and refuses "Charities," "Charitable Foundation," and "Foundation" unless the filer is a registered nonprofit or charitable organization. A reservation under § 31B-1-106 runs 120 days and may be renewed once for a further 120 days, after which the same or associated persons may not reserve the name again within one calendar year of the last reservation's expiry. The LLC formation fee is $100 and an annual report ($25) is due between January 1 and June 30. Filings run through the West Virginia One Stop Business Portal.
